# Let's chat about a vibe-coding (🪱)

![](images/module3/castle_vibe.gif){width=50%}
## Rationale

## _Fact - A:_ Coding is a gateway to lots of tools

It gives you access to...

- Thousands of specialised R packages
- Geospatial tools such as QGIS and PostGIS
- Statistical and biometrics methods that are often only available through code
- Access to database and data engineering tools

## _Fact - B:_ LLMs can write really good code (Module1) 

(_We discussed in module 1 so will not dwell on..._)

__Advantages__

- Trained on billions of lines of code, documentation, tutorials, and technical discussions
- Have "seen" solutions to many common programming problems before
- Can generate working code in seconds
- Often better at spotting syntax errors than average programmers
- Can use thousands of packages and functions that no human could memorise
- coding is very logical/systematic...(perfect for machines)


## _Fact - C:_ You have lots of potentially great ideas

![](images/module3/castle_ideas.gif){width=50%}

Coming up lots of ideas is often easy

![](images/module3/image_bike.jpg){width=50%}

But "testing riding them" (aka seeing if the idea is actually any good) can be a hurdle to every exploring them.



![](images/module3/image_bike_uphill.jpg){width=50%}


## Given __Fact A__ and __Fact B__, why not have LLMs write code for you so you can test ride those ideas (__Fact C__)?

Using LLM to write lowers the cost of "testing riding them"

![](images/module3/image_ebike_uphill.jpg){width=50%}



## What is vibe-coding?


As with lots of terminology in the AI boom, defining vibe-coding is a bit nebulous. Different people (and bots!) use the term differently. For our purposes, let's keep it simple:

__Vibe-coding is a workflow where you describe what you want in natural language, an LLM writes the code, and you iteratively refine the result until you achieve the desired outcome in a reproducible way.__


![](images/module3/image_vibe_coding.jpg){width=40%}


## Caveats with vibe-coding

Vibe-coding can be incredibly productive, but it comes with risks...

- failing into the trap of intellectual laziness
- accept incorrect results in which is the logic does not make sense
- use inappropriate statistical or analytical methods

![](images/module3/image_ebike_cliff.jpg){width=50%}


# Implementing a vibe-coding workflow

## Rationale

Some attributes of a good workflow for vibe-coding...

- reproducible
- makes it efficient to review the code and outputs
- aligns with the coding skills and workflow that are already in-house (@ARI)
- leverages proven workflows


## Example Rstudio/R workflow

Here, we will implement vibe-coding within Rstudio environment (which we have presented previously in our workshops😁)

<aside>Feel free to check our [2024 workshop](https://bfanson.github.io/2024_DADA_workshop/sessions/day1-getting-data-into-shape/) for more details on</aside>


Reminder of key aspects of this workflow...

- Projects (called Rprojects with ext .Rproj ) are the basis

- Structure of directory like the following...

![](images/module3/dir_rproject.png){width=50%}

Key bits...

- `data/`  folder is treated as locked [do not edit]

- `R/` folder holds your scripts [aka documentation of your steps/logic]


## Other workflows exist?

Yes, lots...

honestly, we do not keep track of but between other programming languages (e.g. Python, C++) and LLMs studios (e.g. Claude Code, Codex) and bespoke software, there are lots.

Of course, what we say here on <span style="color: blue;">20 October 2026</span> may be antiquated in a year (...as well as lots of other way we do things😕).

### Summary table of insights...

| Model | \~Cost | Thoughts |
|:--|:--|:--|
| Claude Sonnet (1.0x)  | $3.16 | More expensive model but it viewed the png file with no issues and just needed to ask a few questions.  It was able to evaluate how well it had done and fix several components |
| GLM 5.3 (0.6x) | $1.00 | Not able to "view" the png so that limiting.  After answering a suite of queries the basics were there but it needed much more guidance|
| Claude Haiku (0.4x)  | $x.xx | Least expensive model I tried. |

# Coming back to vibe-coding idea

## Some final thoughts

_Disclaimer: This is us free-thinking in real time during a paradign shift. Feel free to disagree or contribute your own thoughts._

### Resist intellectual laziness

This is not a flippant statement.

As AI tools become more capable, there is a risk that we outsource not only the coding, but also the thinking.

Contributing factors:

- We are increasingly time-stressed.
- Projects often have unrealistic deadlines.
- Vibe-coding can create psychological distance from the underlying problem.
- Modern digital platforms reward speed, visibility, and confidence more than deep understanding.
- AI can produce plausible outputs that reduce the incentive to question assumptions or verify results.

__Key message:__ The danger is not that AI writes code. The danger is that we stop engaging critically with the problem we are trying to solve.


### Reviewing the code

- Despite the temptation, we are going to need to be disciplined about reading the code and ensure 
that we understand exactly what it is doing.

- Not all code requires the same level of assessment (importing data vs ggplot vs statistical analysis)

- Learning how to QC/QA your code and outputs will increase in importance

- As noted, I have a STYLE.MD guide that writes the code in my style.  That helps me review/evaluate the code quicker.


### Learning from vibe-coding

- New approaches to tackling a problem (plan mode)

- Reading the code that the Agent wrote introduced me to new functions/approaches to making new maps


### Beyond spatial data

- Obviously, __vibe-coding is not restricted to spatial data__ and you can implement the same approach to other type of data.


### Homogensing workflow (the future)

An emerging question that we are wondering about (and we mentioned in module 1...sorry to dwell) is what does this mean for how we tackle these steps in the future and our workflows.  

How homogenized do our workflows become?  

  - Standardised ARI STYLE.MD, WOKFLOW.MD, and set of SKILLS.MD files/folders.  
  - Do we have a project folder that has a similar structure so both humans and a local LLM that has been trained on our workflow can easily understand it, revise, and QC it?


All of this seems apt given all the discussion on templates/standardisation
